correctness.rationale: PASS: Differentiating f=x0 u^2+2 x1 u v+x2 v^2 (char k !=2) yields J=(u^2,uv,v^2,x0u+x1v,x1u+x2v). Let A=k[x0,x1,x2], M=(u,v)/J; the graded A-presentation A(-2)^2 -> A(-1)^2 -> M has 2x2 determinant Delta=x0x2-x1^2, nonzero in A, proving injection, Hilbert series 2t/(1-t)^2 and S/J=A⊕M, giving (1+2t-2t^2)/(1-t)^3. Explicit map u->x1, v->-x0 shows M is the ideal (x0,x1) in B=A/(Delta), sheaf O_C(-p)=O_{P1}(-1); it is torsion-free rank one on smooth C and square-zero as nilpotents. Hence associated primes are (u,v) and its embedded (u,v,Delta), the ideal is saturated and J=(u,v)∩(J+(Delta)), and depth equals min(3,2)=2. The projective chart f/unit=U^2+T v^2 proves Whitney umbrella on C, transverse normal crossings off C. Independently verified derivative/determinant identities symbolically and exact modular 101 quotient dimensions d=1,..,6 equal 5,10,16,23,31,40. Infinite claims are algebraic, not inferred from those six degrees.
